units.summary: Open only when button bit $20 is present and latch $52 is zero. Initialize modal controller state, save OAM and two work pages, hide sprites and build its cursor. Reset MMC1 shift state, choose pattern services4/0, set nametable and vertical scroll shadows, then draw the settings fields. Edit speed, confirmation and optionally the secondary field based on $0313; negative confirmation loops back. Reinitialize the display and wait on exit. The exit restores saved OAM and working pages before returning to the battle controller.

phase1.evidence: Bounded direct control-flow from saved accepted opcode roots. See analysis/round1/contracts-battle/static-contract-proof.json and static-contract-instructions.json. Structural inference; no natural execution claim for Static bytes.

units.name: OpenBattleSettingsModal
units.summary: Open only when button bit $20 is present and latch $52 is zero. Initialize modal controller state, save OAM and two work pages, hide sprites and build its cursor. Reset MMC1 shift state, choose pattern services4/0, set nametable and vertical scroll shadows, then draw the settings fields. Edit speed, confirmation and optionally the secondary field based on $0313; negative confirmation loops back. Reinitialize the display and wait on exit. The exit restores saved OAM and working pages before returning to the battle controller.

units.name: WriteBattlePpuRecordStream
units.summary: Interpret records through the A/X pointer until leading $FF. Each record contains flagged PPU high address, low address and byte count. High flag bit7 selects PPU increment32 versus1; bit6 selects repeated fill versus literal bytes. Mask address high to six bits, reset the PPU latch, write the destination and stream the payload. Advance the source pointer after each header/payload segment. If the last high address is $3F, perform the palette-address exit sequence before returning. Count zero wraps to256 writes; ordinary records must use the supported nonzero count contract.

Count zero wraps to256 writes; ordinary records must use the supported nonzero count contract.

Indexed $7100 is actor records here, while unindexed $7100 is also the pending command count; the two access patterns must remain distinct.

regions.summary: Part of WriteSetupPpuPacketStream; see its source contract.

units.name: WriteSetupPpuPacketStream
units.summary: Disable NMI/rendering, then consume PPU packets through $2C/$2D until leading $FF. Flag bit7 selects increment32; flag bit6 selects literal bytes when set and a repeated fill byte otherwise. This differs from the tactical-bank packet consumer. Mask destination high to six bits, reset the PPU latch, write the byte count and advance the source across page boundaries after each header/payload. Count zero produces256 writes. Preserve the original pointer/carry conventions in the two payload paths.

units.name: ServiceAudioChannelsAndRequests
units.summary: Visit eight logical tracks through offset table $835A, retaining their enable bits in $FB and updating active tracks. Consume the pending sound queue in increasing request order while decrementing its count. Fold logical enables into four APU channel bits, then copy the four channel shadows at $06F0 to pulse/triangle/noise registers. Control registers are always refreshed; sweep/timer writes occur only when dirty flag $06EC+channel is zero, then mark it one.

Count down note duration; while nonzero, advance the envelope only on its own timer expiry. At note expiry reset envelope cursor and sweep shadow, interpret high-bit control tokens until a note byte, look up its low-nibble period and shift by the high-nibble octave. Save the advanced stream pointer, apply envelope and update APU shadow only if this track is not masked by the overlay track.

phase1.evidence: Context-aware direct control flow from validated fetch roots/direct JSR callee entry. Calls anchor targets before callee bank effects; return continuation not assumed. Safe indexed RAM writes (base plus full 8-bit index below mapper space) independently preserve mapping. See extend-*.json.

units.summary: Selector $0394 chooses a directory word at $8100. Read its leading remaining-byte count, initialize message PPU cursor $268C and retain the row origin. Emit tile-coded bytes through synchronized PPU services; selector0 prints groups of three and advances the PPU low byte by3, other selectors print one at a time. Selector1 can stop on directional/action input. Token $FF consumes a newline and advances the saved row origin by $20; update the stream pointer by the consumed bytes with high carry. Completion and newline paths restore display state through fixed services.

units.name: BuildTacticalEncounterDescriptors
units.summary: Save center/selected neighbor terrain bytes at $6FFE/$6FFF and copy the selected eight-byte unit buffer to $7000. Neighbor selector $0414 indexes signed byte coordinate offsets; add them to position $04/$05 and search the world unit list for exactly matching low-five-bit X and Y. Copy the matched record to $7008. No match enters a deliberate infinite loop at $B390, making coordinate-consistent target existence a strict caller precondition. This explains why relocated tactical mirrors can animate yet fail world commit later.

After eight counts, move logical cursor one cell and its two-sprite marker by16 vertical or24 horizontal pixels; the marker pair keeps an8-pixel Y separation. At the fixed marker origin ($46 vertical/$68 horizontal), call one-cell viewport scrolling before adjusting the logical position. The direction-specific tails now rejoin the classified common movement/return paths. Finally copy cursor coordinates to logical tile-address inputs and compute its PPU address.

After eight counts, move logical cursor one cell and its two-sprite marker by16 vertical or24 horizontal pixels; the marker pair keeps an8-pixel Y separation. At the fixed marker origin ($46 vertical/$68 horizontal), call one-cell viewport scrolling before adjusting the logical position. The direction-specific tails now rejoin the classified common movement/return paths. Finally copy cursor coordinates to logical tile-address inputs and compute its PPU address.

units.name: BuildFieldNeighborPpuAddresses
units.summary: Build seven PPU address pairs around the logical cursor. Opposite coordinate parity makes all14 bytes $FF; matching parity retains the center and computes the six hex-like neighboring positions using offsets-$80,-$43,-$3D,+$3D,+$43,+$80 with row/circular-field corrections. Stage header edges suppress off-map neighbors by setting $FF pairs. Save/restore the original current tile address so building neighbors has no lasting cursor-address mutation. The table order is three upper entries, center, three lower entries.

units.summary: Entry at $F84F fills X bytes with A through pointer $82/$83, using byte Y; X=0 fills256 bytes. Adjacent reset entry clears all zero page, clears pages $0300..$07FF through that fill helper, then initializes PPUCTRL shadow/hardware to8 and PPUMASK to0. Stack page and OAM page are not part of these clearing loops.

regions.summary: Part of PollFieldControllersAndDecodeEdges; see its source contract.

units.name: PollFieldControllersAndDecodeEdges
units.summary: Read eight serial bits from each standard controller port into $0305/$0306, combining the two low hardware data bits. Active player0 uses port1; player1 ultimately uses port2. Its intermediate port1-mask calculation is overwritten before the active byte store, so no mixed-port input is claimed. Other player values leave active input zero for synthetic control. Convert low directional nibble through $FAA9 and produce a new-direction code only when previous direction was zero. Derive Start/Select press pulses and A/B held plus first-press flags using per-button latches; each release clears its latch. Preserve these actual byte-level rules rather than treating all flags as equivalent input edges.

Its intermediate port1-mask calculation is overwritten before the active byte store, so no mixed-port input is claimed. Other player values leave active input zero for synthetic control. Convert low directional nibble through $FAA9 and produce a new-direction code only when previous direction was zero. Derive Start/Select press pulses and A/B held plus first-press flags using per-button latches; each release clears its latch. Preserve these actual byte-level rules rather than treating all flags as equivalent input edges.
